question: Which among the following rulers adopted the title devaputra?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kushana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Kushana rulers adopted the grand title Devaputra meaning "son of god". (देवपुत्र — ईश्वर का पुत्र)

• Kanishka and other Kushana kings used a string of titles borrowed from many cultures — Maharaja, Rajatiraja (king of kings, from Persia), Devaputra (from China, where the emperor was called Son of Heaven) and Kaisara (from the Roman Caesar).

• Kanishka I (c. 78 CE) was the greatest Kushana ruler; he convened the Fourth Buddhist Council in Kashmir and patronised the Gandhara and Mathura schools of art.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Hoysalas ruled Karnataka (capital Dwarasamudra/Halebidu) and built the Chennakeshava temple at Belur.

• Cholas used titles such as Parakesarivarman and Rajakesarivarman.

• Sakas (Indo-Scythians) used Kshatrapa and Mahakshatrapa; Rudradaman I is famous for the Junagadh rock inscription.

NOTE

• Kushana gold coinage was the purest in ancient India; Kanishka's coins bear images of Buddha.

• The Saka era (78 CE) is the national calendar of India and is usually linked to Kanishka's accession.

question: What was the theme of International Yoga Day (2022)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Yoga for Humanity.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The theme of the 8th International Day of Yoga (21 June 2022) was "Yoga for Humanity". (मानवता के लिए योग)

• The main national event of 2022 was held at the Mysuru Palace grounds, Karnataka, led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, along with the "Guardian Ring" programme spanning 79 countries.

• International Day of Yoga is observed every year on 21 June — the summer solstice, the longest day in the Northern Hemisphere.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The UN General Assembly declared 21 June as International Yoga Day on 11 December 2014, following India's proposal made by PM Modi in September 2014; the resolution had a record 177 co-sponsors.

• Theme 2021 — "Yoga for Wellness"; 2023 — "Yoga for Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam"; 2024 — "Yoga for Self and Society".

NOTE

• Yoga is one of the six orthodox (astika) schools of Indian philosophy; Patanjali's Yoga Sutras is its foundational text.

• The Ministry of AYUSH is the nodal ministry for Yoga in India.

question: Basketball game is played between two teams of ______ players each.
solution_text:
The correct answer is five.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Basketball is played between two teams of five players each on court, with substitutes on the bench. (बास्केटबॉल — प्रत्येक टीम में 5 खिलाड़ी)

• The game was invented by Dr James Naismith in 1891 at Springfield, Massachusetts, USA.

• A standard FIBA match has 4 quarters of 10 minutes each; the basket/ring is fixed at a height of 10 feet (3.05 m).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Number of players per side in other games: Volleyball – 6, Kabaddi – 7, Hockey/Football – 11, Kho-Kho – 9 (12 in a team), Water polo – 7, Netball – 7.

• The world governing body of basketball is FIBA (International Basketball Federation), founded 1932, headquartered at Mies, Switzerland.

NOTE

• Basketball terms: dribble, dunk, rebound, pivot, lay-up, free throw, alley-oop.

• The Basketball Federation of India (BFI) governs the sport in India; basketball became an Olympic sport in 1936 (Berlin).

question: According to the first National Multidimensional Poverty Index by NITI Aayog, which state has the maximum percentage of poor people?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• NITI Aayog released India's first National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) baseline report in November 2021, based on NFHS-4 (2015-16) data.

• Bihar had the highest proportion of multidimensionally poor people (about 51.91%), followed by Jharkhand, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh. (बहुआयामी गरीबी सूचकांक)

• Kerala recorded the lowest incidence of multidimensional poverty, followed by Goa, Sikkim and Tamil Nadu.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The National MPI uses 3 dimensions — Health, Education and Standard of Living — and 12 indicators, following the globally accepted Alkire-Foster methodology (OPHI and UNDP).

• MPI value = Headcount ratio (H) × Intensity of poverty (A).

NOTE

• NITI Aayog was formed on 1 January 2015, replacing the Planning Commission; the Prime Minister is its Chairperson.

• Global MPI is published jointly by UNDP and the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI).

question: Editor of a Marathi newspaper “Kesari” was ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bal Gangadhar Tilak.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bal Gangadhar Tilak started and edited the Marathi weekly Kesari (meaning "lion") and the English weekly Maratha in 1881. (केसरी — मराठी समाचार पत्र)

• Through Kesari he spread nationalist ideas and gave the famous slogan "Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it".

• He was called "Lokmanya" and was described by the British as the "Father of Indian Unrest"; he began the Ganapati (1893) and Shivaji (1895) festivals to build mass nationalism.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Bipin Chandra Pal — edited New India and Bande Mataram; part of the Lal-Bal-Pal trio.

• Aurobindo Ghosh — associated with Bande Mataram, Karmayogin and Dharma.

• Lala Lajpat Rai — published Young India, The People and Vande Mataram (Urdu).

NOTE

• Tilak wrote Gita Rahasya and The Arctic Home in the Vedas while imprisoned in Mandalay (1908-14).

• He co-founded the All India Home Rule League (1916) with Annie Besant.

question: In which of the following articles, “Right of minorities to establish and administer educational institution” is mentioned?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 30.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 30 of the Indian Constitution gives all religious and linguistic minorities the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice. (अल्पसंख्यकों का शिक्षा संस्थान स्थापित करने का अधिकार)

• It falls under the Cultural and Educational Rights (Articles 29-30), a part of the Fundamental Rights in Part III of the Constitution.

• Article 30(2) bars the State from discriminating against any educational institution while granting aid on the ground that it is managed by a minority.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Article 29 — protection of the language, script and culture of any section of citizens, and no denial of admission to State-aided institutions on grounds of religion, race, caste or language.

• Article 28 — no religious instruction in wholly State-funded educational institutions.

• Article 31 (Right to Property) was repealed by the 44th Amendment, 1978; it is now a legal right under Article 300A.

NOTE

• Fundamental Rights are contained in Articles 12-35 and there are six of them today.

• Article 21A (added by the 86th Amendment, 2002) makes free and compulsory education for children aged 6-14 a fundamental right.

question: The broad, green part of the leaf is called ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is lamina.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The lamina (also called the leaf blade) is the broad, flat, green expanded part of a leaf where photosynthesis mainly takes place. (पर्ण फलक)

• Its green colour comes from chlorophyll present in the chloroplasts of the mesophyll cells.

• A typical leaf has three parts — leaf base, petiole and lamina.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Petiole — the stalk that attaches the leaf blade to the stem and holds the lamina in light; a leaf without a petiole is called sessile.

• Midrib — the thick central vein running through the middle of the lamina.

• Veins — the network of vascular tissue (xylem and phloem) that transports water and food and gives the leaf rigidity.

NOTE

• The design of veins on the lamina is called venation — reticulate in dicots (e.g. mango, peepal) and parallel in monocots (e.g. grass, banana).

• Exchange of gases and transpiration occur through tiny pores on the leaf called stomata, guarded by guard cells.

question: According to ______ law, heat produced by an electric current is directly proportional to the resistance of the conductor, the square of the current, and the time for which it flows.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Joule's.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Joule's law of heating states that the heat produced in a conductor is H = I²Rt, i.e. directly proportional to the square of the current (I²), the resistance (R) and the time (t). (जूल का तापन नियम)

• It was given by the English physicist James Prescott Joule; the SI unit of energy, the joule (J), is named after him.

• Practical applications: electric heater, electric iron, geyser, toaster, incandescent bulb and electric fuse.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Hooke's law — within the elastic limit, stress is directly proportional to strain (F = -kx).

• Charles's law — at constant pressure, the volume of a fixed mass of gas is directly proportional to its absolute temperature (V ∝ T).

• Faraday's laws — of electromagnetic induction (induced emf ∝ rate of change of magnetic flux) and of electrolysis.

NOTE

• The heating element of appliances is made of nichrome, because of its high resistivity and high melting point and because it does not oxidise readily.

• Ohm's law: V = IR (at constant temperature).

question: The Ilbert Bill was passed during the term of Lord Ripon to bring Indian and European magistracy on equal footing in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1883.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Ilbert Bill was introduced in 1883 during the viceroyalty of Lord Ripon (1880-84), drafted by the law member Sir Courtenay Peregrine Ilbert. (इल्बर्ट बिल — 1883)

• It sought to allow Indian judges and magistrates to try Europeans in criminal cases, removing the racial disqualification in the judiciary.

• Fierce agitation by the European community in India forced the government to amend/dilute the Bill in 1884, allowing a European accused the right to trial by a jury with at least half Europeans.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The white agitation exposed British racism and gave Indians a lesson in organised protest — it is regarded as one of the immediate factors leading to the founding of the Indian National Congress in 1885.

• Other measures of Lord Ripon: repeal of the Vernacular Press Act (1882), the Local Self-Government Resolution (1882) — he is called the "Father of Local Self-Government in India" — the First Factory Act (1881) and the Hunter Commission on education (1882).

NOTE

• Vernacular Press Act (1878) and Arms Act (1878) were passed by Lord Lytton.

• The Indian Councils Act, 1892 was passed during the term of Lord Lansdowne.

question: The Khangchendzonga Biosphere Reserve is located in which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sikkim.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Khangchendzonga Biosphere Reserve lies in the state of Sikkim, around Mount Kanchenjunga, the highest peak in India and the third highest in the world (8,586 m). (कंचनजंगा जैवमंडल रिज़र्व — सिक्किम)

• It was designated a Biosphere Reserve in 2000 and added to the UNESCO Man and the Biosphere (MAB) World Network in 2018.

• Khangchendzonga National Park within it became India's first "Mixed" UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2016 (natural + cultural criteria).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Biosphere reserves in the North-East: Nokrek (Meghalaya), Manas and Dibru-Saikhowa (Assam), Dihang-Dibang (Arunachal Pradesh).

• Kerala shares the Agasthyamala and Nilgiri biosphere reserves; the Nilgiri (1986) was India's first biosphere reserve.

NOTE

• India has 18 biosphere reserves, of which 12 are on the UNESCO MAB list.

• A biosphere reserve has three zones — core, buffer and transition.

question: Seasonal reversal in the wind direction during a year refers to______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Monsoon.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word monsoon comes from the Arabic word "mausim", meaning season, and refers to the seasonal reversal in the wind direction during a year. (मानसून — हवाओं की मौसमी उलटफेर)

• In summer, winds blow from sea to land (South-West monsoon, June-September) bringing rain; in winter they blow from land to sea (North-East/retreating monsoon).

• The reversal is caused by the differential heating of land and sea, the shift of the ITCZ, the Tibetan plateau heating and the jet streams.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Breeze — a gentle local wind; land breeze blows at night from land to sea and sea breeze during the day from sea to land.

• Climate is the average of weather conditions over a long period (about 30 years), whereas weather is the day-to-day state of the atmosphere.

NOTE

• India's monsoon normally arrives over Kerala around 1 June and withdraws by mid-September to October.

• The two branches of the South-West monsoon are the Arabian Sea branch and the Bay of Bengal branch; Mawsynram (Meghalaya) receives the highest rainfall in the world.

question: Kumari Kamala was awarded with Padma Bhushan in 1970. She is a preeminent artist of the ______ tradition of the dance.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vazhuvoor.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kumari Kamala (Kamala Lakshman) is a celebrated Bharatanatyam dancer and film actress, a foremost exponent of the Vazhuvoor style/bani of Bharatanatyam. (वझुवूर शैली — भरतनाट्यम)

• She was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 1970 and learnt under Vazhuvoor Ramaiah Pillai, the guru who gave the style its name.

• The Vazhuvoor bani is known for its graceful, rounded movements, delicate abhinaya and dramatic presentation, and is one of the main styles (banis) of Bharatanatyam along with Pandanallur, Thanjavur and Melattur.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Kuchipudi is the classical dance of Andhra Pradesh, developed by Siddhendra Yogi; exponents include Raja and Radha Reddy and Yamini Krishnamurthy.

• Tamzara is a folk dance of Armenian/Anatolian origin, and Kurdish dance belongs to the Kurdish people of West Asia — neither is an Indian classical tradition.

NOTE

• India has 8 classical dances — Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (UP), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

• Bharatanatyam is based on the Natya Shastra of Bharat Muni and was earlier called Sadir/Dasiattam.

question: The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2022 is awarded to ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Svante Paabo.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 2022 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded to the Swedish geneticist Svante Pääbo for his discoveries concerning the genomes of extinct hominins and human evolution. (मानव विकास और विलुप्त होमिनिन के जीनोम)

• He sequenced the Neanderthal genome and discovered a previously unknown hominin, the Denisova, and founded the discipline of paleogenomics.

• His father, Sune Bergström, had won the same prize in 1982 — making them one of the few parent-child Nobel pairs.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Ales Bialiatski (Belarus) shared the 2022 Nobel Peace Prize with Russia's Memorial and Ukraine's Center for Civil Liberties.

• Giorgia Meloni became the Prime Minister of Italy in October 2022 — its first woman PM.

• Valeri Polyakov was the Russian cosmonaut who holds the record for the longest single stay in space (437 days).

NOTE

• Nobel Prizes were instituted by Alfred Nobel and first awarded in 1901; the Economics prize was added in 1969 by the Sveriges Riksbank.

• The Medicine prize is awarded by the Karolinska Institute, Stockholm.

question: The Vadhavan Port is located in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Vadhavan Port is being developed near Dahanu in Palghar district of Maharashtra, on the Arabian Sea coast. (वाढवण बंदरगाह — महाराष्ट्र)

• The Union Cabinet approved its development as an all-weather greenfield deep-draft major port; it is being built by the Vadhavan Port Project Ltd (VPPL), a JV of Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority (JNPA) and the Maharashtra Maritime Board.

• Its natural draft of about 20 metres will let it handle the largest container ships and place it among the top 10 container ports of the world.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Other major ports of Maharashtra: Mumbai Port and Jawaharlal Nehru Port (Nhava Sheva) — the largest container-handling port in India.

• Kerala — Kochi and Vizhinjam ports; Tamil Nadu — Chennai, Ennore (Kamarajar) and V.O. Chidambaranar (Tuticorin); West Bengal — Kolkata (Syama Prasad Mookerjee) Port.

NOTE

• India has a coastline of about 7,500 km with 12 major ports plus a large number of non-major ports.

• Kandla (Deendayal) Port in Gujarat is a tidal port; Paradip is in Odisha and Mormugao in Goa.

question: The Kuiper Belt is a ring of icy rocks & dust bodies just outside the orbit of ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Neptune.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Kuiper Belt is a doughnut-shaped ring of icy bodies, rocks and dust lying just beyond the orbit of Neptune, roughly 30 to 50 AU from the Sun. (कुइपर बेल्ट — नेप्च्यून की कक्षा के बाहर)

• Objects in it are called Kuiper Belt Objects (KBOs) or trans-Neptunian objects; Pluto is the largest and best-known, along with Haumea, Makemake and Eris.

• It is named after the Dutch-American astronomer Gerard Kuiper, and is considered the source of many short-period comets.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The asteroid belt lies between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter — do not confuse it with the Kuiper Belt.

• The Oort Cloud is a far more distant spherical shell of icy bodies surrounding the solar system, the source of long-period comets.

• NASA's New Horizons mission flew past Pluto in 2015 and the KBO Arrokoth in 2019.

NOTE

• Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet by the IAU in 2006.

• Neptune is the farthest planet from the Sun and was discovered in 1846; it is called the windiest planet.

question: The Merdeka Cup is associated with which of the following sports?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Football.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Merdeka Cup (Merdeka Tournament) is an international football tournament hosted by Malaysia, started in 1957 to mark the country's independence — "Merdeka" means independence/freedom in Malay. (मर्डेका कप — फुटबॉल)

• India won the Merdeka Cup in 1959 and finished runner-up on several occasions during the golden era of Indian football.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Other football trophies: Durand Cup (oldest in Asia, 1888), Santosh Trophy, Rovers Cup, Subroto Cup, DCM Trophy, FIFA World Cup, Copa America.

• Hockey trophies: Agha Khan Cup, Dhyan Chand Trophy, Beighton Cup, Rangaswami Cup, Azlan Shah Cup (also hosted by Malaysia).

• Chess: Candidates Tournament, Chess Olympiad (44th edition held at Chennai, 2022); Golf: Ryder Cup, Walker Cup, Masters.

NOTE

• The governing body of world football is FIFA (founded 1904, HQ Zurich); Indian football is run by the AIFF (1937).

• The FIFA World Cup 2022 was held in Qatar and won by Argentina.

question: Which of the following is NOT part of six school of Indian Philosophy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dravida.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The six orthodox (astika) schools of Indian philosophy — Shad-darshana are Samkhya, Yoga, Nyaya, Vaisheshika, Mimamsa (Purva Mimamsa) and Vedanta (Uttara Mimamsa). (षड्दर्शन)

• Dravida is not a school of philosophy — it refers to a language family/region of South India, so it is the odd one out.

• Founders: Samkhya — Kapila, Yoga — Patanjali, Nyaya — Gautama (Akshapada), Vaisheshika — Kanada, Mimamsa — Jaimini, Vedanta — Badarayana (Vyasa).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Samkhya is the oldest school and is dualistic — Purusha (consciousness) and Prakriti (matter).

• Nyaya is the school of logic, whose text is the Nyaya Sutra; Vaisheshika proposed the atomic (paramanu) theory of matter.

• Heterodox (nastika) schools that reject Vedic authority: Buddhism, Jainism, Charvaka (Lokayata), Ajivika.

NOTE

• Schools are paired traditionally: Samkhya-Yoga, Nyaya-Vaisheshika, Mimamsa-Vedanta.

• Adi Shankaracharya propounded Advaita Vedanta; Ramanuja — Vishishtadvaita; Madhvacharya — Dvaita.

question: Indian economy is seen growing at ______ per cent in the current fiscal, finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said while presenting the Union Budget 2022.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 9.2.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• While presenting the Union Budget 2022-23 on 1 February 2022, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said the Indian economy was estimated to grow at 9.2 per cent in the then current fiscal (FY 2021-22), the highest among all large economies. (केंद्रीय बजट 2022-23)

• This was based on the First Advance Estimates of the National Statistical Office and reflected the rebound after the COVID-19 contraction of FY 2020-21.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Key announcements of Budget 2022-23: PM GatiShakti master plan with 7 engines, Digital Rupee (CBDC) by the RBI, 30% tax on income from virtual digital assets, PM Awas Yojana allocation, Vibrant Villages Programme, Ken-Betwa river linking project and 400 new Vande Bharat trains.

• It was Nirmala Sitharaman's fourth consecutive budget, presented in paperless form through the Union Budget Mobile App.

NOTE

• The Union Budget is presented under Article 112 (Annual Financial Statement) of the Constitution.

• R.K. Shanmukham Chetty presented India's first budget (1947); Morarji Desai presented the maximum number of budgets.

question: According to the Mediation Bill, 2021, the mediation process must be completed within 180 days, which may be extended by another ______ days by the parties.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 180.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Mediation Bill, 2021 (introduced in the Rajya Sabha in December 2021) provided that the mediation process must be completed within 180 days, extendable by another 180 days if the parties agree. (मध्यस्थता विधेयक, 2021)

• The Bill made pre-litigation mediation a step before approaching a court, and provided for the registration of the mediated settlement agreement with legal enforceability like a court decree.

• It also proposed setting up the Mediation Council of India and provided for Online Mediation and community mediation.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• A party may withdraw from mediation after the first two sessions.

• The Bill was later enacted as the Mediation Act, 2023, which reduced the mediation period to 120 days, extendable by 60 days.

NOTE

• Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) methods include arbitration, conciliation, mediation, negotiation and Lok Adalat.

• Section 89 of the CPC, 1908 and Article 39A (free legal aid) support ADR in India.

question: The six – day Khajuraho Dance festival is celebrated in which of the following state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Khajuraho Dance Festival is a week-long (six-day) festival of Indian classical dance held every year in February-March at Khajuraho in Chhatarpur district, Madhya Pradesh. (खजुराहो नृत्य महोत्सव — मध्य प्रदेश)

• It is organised by the Kala evam Sahitya Parishad, Madhya Pradesh, against the backdrop of the Khajuraho group of temples, built by the Chandela rulers between the 9th and 11th centuries.

• The Khajuraho temples were declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986; the Kandariya Mahadev temple is the largest of them.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other festivals of Madhya Pradesh: Tansen Samaroh (Gwalior), Lokrang, Malwa Utsav, Bhagoria.

• Dance festivals elsewhere: Konark Dance Festival (Odisha), Mamallapuram Dance Festival (Tamil Nadu), Elephanta Festival (Maharashtra), Nishagandhi (Kerala).

NOTE

• Madhya Pradesh has three UNESCO World Heritage Sites — Khajuraho, the Buddhist Monuments at Sanchi and the Bhimbetka rock shelters.

• Khajuraho temples are built in the Nagara style of temple architecture.

question: The first population census in India was conducted in _______ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1872.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The first population census in India was conducted in 1872 during the viceroyalty of Lord Mayo; it was non-synchronous, i.e. carried out in different parts at different times. (भारत की पहली जनगणना — 1872)

• The first synchronous (complete) census was held in 1881 under Lord Ripon, guided by W.C. Plowden, the Census Commissioner of India.

• Since 1881, the census has been conducted every ten years without a break until 2011.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Census 2011 was the 15th census since 1872 and the 7th after Independence; its theme was "Our Census, Our Future".

• As per Census 2011: population 121.08 crore, density 382 persons/sq km, sex ratio 943, literacy rate 74.04% (Kerala highest, Bihar lowest).

NOTE

• The census is conducted by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India under the Ministry of Home Affairs, as per the Census Act, 1948.

• Uttar Pradesh is the most populous state; Sikkim the least populous; Bihar the most densely populated.

question: Sri Deepak Mazumdar received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for the year ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2018.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sri Deepak Mazumdar, an eminent Bharatanatyam dancer from Maharashtra, was conferred the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for the year 2018. (संगीत नाटक अकादमी पुरस्कार)

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi Award is India's highest national recognition given to performing artists in the fields of music, dance, theatre, puppetry and traditional/folk arts.

• The award carries Rs 1,00,000, an Angavastram and a Tamrapatra (brass plaque).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's National Academy of Music, Dance and Drama, was set up in 1952-53 and is headquartered in New Delhi; it is the oldest of the national academies.

• Its highest honour is the Akademi Ratna (Fellowship), limited to 40 living fellows at a time.

NOTE

• Other national academies: Sahitya Akademi (literature, 1954) and Lalit Kala Akademi (fine arts, 1954), both in New Delhi.

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi Amrit Award was instituted in 2022 for artists above 75 who had not received the award earlier.

question: Who among the following built the Hawa Mahal in Jaipur?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Hawa Mahal ("Palace of Winds") in Jaipur, Rajasthan was built in 1799 by Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh, a grandson of Sawai Jai Singh II. (हवा महल — जयपुर)

• It was designed by the architect Lal Chand Ustad in the shape of the crown of Lord Krishna, and is made of red and pink sandstone.

• It has 953 small windows (jharokhas) with intricate latticework, which allowed royal ladies observing purdah to watch street processions unseen, while keeping the interior cool by the Venturi effect.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Raja Man Singh I was the Kachwaha ruler of Amber and one of the navratnas of Akbar; he built the Amber Fort palace complex.

• Krishnaraja Wadiyar IV was the Maharaja of Mysore (1902-40), called "Rajarshi" by Mahatma Gandhi.

• Jaipur, the "Pink City", was founded in 1727 by Sawai Jai Singh II, and its walled city became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2019.

NOTE

• Other Jaipur monuments: Jantar Mantar (UNESCO, 2010), City Palace, Amber Fort, Jaigarh and Nahargarh forts.

• Rajasthan's Hill Forts (Chittorgarh, Kumbhalgarh, Ranthambore, Amber, Jaisalmer, Gagron) became a UNESCO site in 2013.

question: Annapurna Devi was known to practice which musical instrument?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Surbahar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Annapurna Devi (1927-2018), born Roshanara Khan, was a legendary player of the surbahar (bass sitar), an instrument of Hindustani classical music. (सुरबहार — बास सितार)

• She was the daughter and disciple of Ustad Allauddin Khan of the Maihar gharana, and was married to sitar maestro Pandit Ravi Shankar.

• She was awarded the Padma Bhushan (1977), the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1991) and the Akademi Fellowship (1999); she largely withdrew from public performance and devoted herself to teaching.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Sarod — Ustad Amjad Ali Khan, Ustad Ali Akbar Khan (her brother), Ustad Hafiz Ali Khan, Buddhadev Das Gupta.

• Violin — Dr L. Subramaniam, M.S. Gopalakrishnan, T.N. Krishnan, Lalgudi Jayaraman.

• Bamboo flute (bansuri) — Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia, Pannalal Ghosh.

NOTE

• Instrument-artist pairs often asked: Sitar — Ravi Shankar, Vilayat Khan; Shehnai — Bismillah Khan; Santoor — Shivkumar Sharma; Tabla — Zakir Hussain, Alla Rakha; Mohan Veena — Vishwa Mohan Bhatt.

• The surbahar is a plucked string (tat vadya) instrument, larger and deeper in tone than the sitar.

question: "India at Risk" is written by which of the following authors?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jaswant Singh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "India at Risk: Mistakes, Misconceptions and Misadventures of Security Policy" was written by Jaswant Singh and published in 2013. (इंडिया एट रिस्क)

• Jaswant Singh (1938-2020) was a senior BJP leader and the only person to have served as India's Finance Minister, External Affairs Minister and Defence Minister.

• His other well-known books include "A Call to Honour: In Service of Emergent India", "Jinnah: India-Partition-Independence" and "Defending India".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Khushwant Singh — "Train to Pakistan", "The Company of Women", "Delhi: A Novel", "Truth, Love and a Little Malice".

• K. Natwar Singh — "One Life is Not Enough", "Walking with Lions", "My China Diary".

• Vijay Darda is a former Rajya Sabha MP and journalist associated with the Lokmat group.

NOTE

• Jaswant Singh was the Indian representative in the Strobe Talbott talks after the 1998 Pokhran-II tests and handled the IC-814 Kandahar hijack episode in 1999.

• Book-author pairs are a recurring SSC topic — revise autobiographies of politicians and sportspersons.
